newsitem.title: USA: SEC enforcement to review Calif muni probe request.
newsitem.headline: SEC enforcement to review Calif muni probe request.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission's chairman said he has forwarded California state Treasurer Matt Fong's request for a probe of certain municipal bond financings to its enforcement division.
SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt said in a letter to Fong, which was obtained by Reuters on Friday, that he forwarded Fong's request to SEC enforcement and municipal securities officials.

In the letter, Levitt said he asked William McLucas of the division of enforcement and Paul Maco of the office of municipal securities to "consider additional ways in which we (the SEC) might be of assistance."
In September, Fong called on the SEC, California's Attorney General and the State Bar of California to investigate nine municipal securities transactions underwritten by Pacific Genesis Group Inc.

In these municipal bond deals, Fong alleged that illegal payments of bond proceeds were made, bond proceeds were used to retire private debts and bond professionals failed to identify the actual project beneficiaries.

The transactions were conducted under the state's Marks-Roos Local Bond Pooling Act, authorizing the formation of joint powers agencies to finance the capital projects of local governments in California.
Levitt thanked Fong for requesting the SEC probe. Levitt said such requests were "an important source for our enforcement inquiries."
Levitt said, however, that it was "commission policy, of course, to neither confirm nor deny that particular matters may be the subject of an investigation."
The State Bar of California said in its letter to Fong that it referred the state treasurer's request to its office of the chief trial counsel for review.
The state's Attorney General said the matter was referred to its government section for investigation and that it had been in contact with the SEC about conducting a joint probe.
